panels.label: Tandy 1000 HX price block, feature bullets, and introduction

figures.caption: The 1988 Tandy catalog advertised the 1000 HX with Personal DeskMate 2 included. Its built-in ROM contained MS-DOS, not an explicitly advertised copy of DeskMate.
figures.alt: 1988 Tandy 1000 HX catalog listing with a $699 price, feature bullets for MS-DOS in ROM and included Personal DeskMate 2, and introductory text.
figures.attribution: Tandy Corporation, 1988 Tandy Computer Catalog and Software Reference Guide, printed p. 9.
figures.rights_status: unresolved; limited historical excerpt pending the operator's publication-rights decision
figures.purpose: Shows that the HX offer paired an MS-DOS ROM with a separately supplied Personal DeskMate 2 package, which the chronology contrasts with the SL's DeskMate-in-ROM claim.
figures.excerpt_rationale: The price block, the MS-DOS and Personal DeskMate 2 bullets, and the introductory paragraph must appear together for the claim to be checkable; the product photograph and the specifications block on the same leaf add no further evidence and are omitted.

panels.label: Color Computer DeskMate, DeskMate II (PC-compatible/2000), and Color Computer 3 DeskMate 3 entries
Tandy Personal DeskMate for the 1000 EX/1000
Tandy Personal DeskMate 2 heading and opening lines (continues at the top of the right column)
Personal DeskMate 2 continuation, price, and bundle note

figures.caption: Radio Shack offered several distinct DeskMate products in its 1988 catalog. The separately listed Color Computer DeskMate 3 belonged to a different platform family.
figures.alt: Catalog clippings of Tandy's 1988 software listings: Color Computer DeskMate, DeskMate II, Color Computer 3 DeskMate 3, Personal DeskMate, Personal DeskMate 2, and Professional DeskMate, with prices and supported computer families.
figures.attribution: Tandy Corporation, 1988 Tandy Computer Catalog and Software Reference Guide, printed pp. 102–103.
figures.rights_status: unresolved; limited historical excerpt pending the operator's publication-rights decision
figures.purpose: Documents the overlapping 1988 retail editions and preserves each product's platform qualifier, catalog number, and price so that the Color Computer and PC-compatible lines are not collapsed into one version sequence.
figures.excerpt_rationale: Five excerpts keep every DeskMate heading, platform qualifier, catalog number, and price while excluding the unrelated Offix, Open Access, PFS, GEM, and Framework entries printed on the same leaves. Personal DeskMate 2 flows from the foot of the left column to the head of the right column, so it is kept as two panels in printed reading order rather than retouched or reflowed.

panels.label: Tandy 1000 SL advertisement headline, machine photograph, and opening copy

figures.caption: In 1988, Tandy advertised the 1000 SL with both MS-DOS and DeskMate in ROM—a distinct arrangement from the HX's DOS-in-ROM bundle.
figures.alt: Period Radio Shack advertisement headed “The New Tandy 1000 SL,” with the claim “Built-in MS-DOS and DeskMate for the ultimate in ease of use,” a photograph of the computer, and body copy describing MS-DOS and DeskMate in ROM.
figures.attribution: Radio Shack advertisement, COMPUTE! Issue 101, October 1988, printed p. 25 (an unnumbered full-page advertisement page).
figures.rights_status: unresolved; limited historical excerpt pending the operator's publication-rights decision
figures.purpose: Shows DeskMate itself advertised as built into the computer's ROM, the counterpoint to the HX's DOS-in-ROM bundle with Personal DeskMate 2 on a separate disk.
figures.excerpt_rationale: The headline claim, the machine photograph, and the opening paragraph that states the ROM arrangement are the evidence; the remaining columns, the catalogue-request coupon, and the rest of the advertisement are omitted.

figures.caption: A surviving Personal DeskMate 2 manual beside a Tandy 1000 TX guide, photographed in a modern collection.
figures.alt: Two spiral-bound Tandy manuals photographed side by side, including the Personal DeskMate 2 cover.
figures.attribution: Photograph by Bill Degnan, vintagecomputer.net; the site states “All Images Copyright Degnan, Co. 1949 – 2026”.
figures.rights_status: external linked reference only; no reproduction basis recorded; do not copy into the repository or the website
figures.purpose: Shows what a buyer received as printed documentation with the Personal DeskMate 2 bundle, which catalog copy alone cannot show.
figures.excerpt_rationale: No local derivative is prepared. The photographer retains copyright, no permission has been sought, and a link with a credit serves the same contextual purpose without reproducing the photograph.

external_inspection.observed: Colour photograph of two spiral-bound manuals; the Personal DeskMate 2 cover faces the camera beside a Tandy 1000 TX guide.
